title: Classification simplicial space and its strict mapping fibers
statement:
Use small quasicategories, functor simplicial sets, equivalence edges, cores and weak homotopy equivalences from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and homotopy Segal spaces from [lem-coef-segal-dk-diagonal-equivalence]. Let $Q$ be any small quasicategory. Define $C(Q)_{p,q}$ to be the set of simplicial maps $u:\Delta^p\times\Delta^q\to Q$ whose restriction to $\{i\}\times\Delta^q$ carries every edge to an equivalence of $Q$, for every vertex $0\leq i\leq p$. Precomposition in the two variables makes $C(Q)$ a bisimplicial set, natural in $Q$. There are natural equalities
$$C(Q)_{p,\bullet}=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^p,Q)^\simeq,\qquad C(Q)_{0,\bullet}=Q^\simeq.$$
Here the superscript denotes the core, consisting of simplices all of whose edges are equivalences. The simplicial space $p\mapsto C(Q)_{p,\bullet}$ is a homotopy Segal space. Its endpoint map $C(Q)_{1,\bullet}\to Q^\simeq\times Q^\simeq$ is a Kan fibration, and its strict fiber over vertices $(x,y)$ is naturally
$$U_Q(x,y)=\{x\}\times_{Q,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,Q)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,Q}\{y\}.$$
Consequently this strict fiber also represents its homotopy fiber. In degree $n$, restrict $u\in C(Q)_{n,n}$ along the diagonal $\Delta^n\to\Delta^n\times\Delta^n$; these restrictions define a natural simplicial map $e_Q:\operatorname{diag}C(Q)\to Q$.

source.place: Section 1 (Theorem 1.9 and Proposition 1.16), Proposition 4.9 and Proposition 4.10: classification diagram r(Q)_p = core Fun(Delta^p,Q) is a complete Segal space; core and quasi-fibration properties give the displayed endpoint fibration and strict fiber. The displayed evaluation map is defined by restriction, not asserted here to be a weak equivalence: that assertion is proved explicitly by two simplicial homotopies in the parent item. Read online; not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag states this theorem.

proof.text: For operators $\alpha:[p']\to[p]$ and $\beta:[q']\to[q]$, send $u$ to $u\circ(\Delta(\alpha)\times\Delta(\beta))$. At a vertex $i'$ the vertical restriction is the restriction of $u$ at $\alpha(i')$, precomposed with $\Delta(\beta)$, so its edges still go to equivalences. Identity and composition of these operators follow from identity and composition of precomposition; the two variables commute. A simplicial map $f:Q\to Q'$ preserves equivalence edges because it sends their inverse edges and both inverse-triangle $2$-simplices to the same witnesses in $Q'$. Thus $u\mapsto fu$ preserves the condition and commutes with both operators, giving the asserted natural bisimplicial set.

proof.text:
For an arbitrary small simplicial set $K$, denote by $Y(K)$ the simplicial set of maps $K	imes\Delta^q	o Q$ which take every edge in each $\{v\}	imes\Delta^q$, $v\in K_0$, to an equivalence. Use the minimal marking $K^ lat$ and the equivalence marking $Q^
atural$ of [lem-coef-marked-anodyne-lifting-calculus]. A marked edge of $K^ lat	imes(\Delta^q)^\sharp$ has constant $K$ coordinate at a vertex, and all such edges are marked. Consequently, degree by degree and with the same operators,
$$Y(K)=\operatorname{Map}^\sharp(K^ lat,Q^
atural).$$
Likewise $\operatorname{Map}^ lat(K^ lat,Q^
atural)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)$: only edges degenerate in both coordinates are marked, and their images are automatically degenerate. The core assertion in that cited statement therefore gives $Y(K)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,Q)^\simeq$ and says it is Kan. Taking $K=\Delta^p$ yields $C(Q)_{p, ullet}=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^p,Q)^\simeq$; for $K=\Delta^0$, evaluation is the natural equality with $Q^\simeq$. The same cited statement says restriction $Y(B)	o Y(A)$ is a Kan fibration for every simplicial subset $A\subseteq B$, since $A^ lat	o B^ lat$ is degreewise injective. In particular $Y(\Delta^1)	o Y(\{0,1\})=Q^\simeq	imes Q^\simeq$, and the restrictions to either endpoint, are Kan fibrations. All equalities commute with restriction in $K$ and postcomposition in $Q$ because they retain exactly the same maps of simplicial sets.

proof.text:
For $n\geq2$ put $S=\operatorname{Sp}[n]\subseteq\Delta^n$, the union of consecutive edges as in [lem-cbc-spine-inner-anodyne]. Gluing maps on these edges identifies
$$Y(S)=P_n:=C(Q)_{1,\bullet}\times_{Q^\simeq}\cdots\times_{Q^\simeq}C(Q)_{1,\bullet}$$
with $n$ factors and strict equality at the matched endpoints. This is degreewise gluing: distinct consecutive edges meet only in their common vertex, and product with $\Delta^m$ preserves this union and its intersections degree by degree. In particular no homotopy pullback has yet been substituted. The endpoint maps are Kan fibrations by step 2, so their iterated strict pullbacks $P_n$ are Kan (horn fillers lift through a pullback); $Y(\Delta^n)$ is Kan by step 2 as well. Prove directly that restriction $r_n:Y(\Delta^n)\to Y(S)$ lifts every boundary $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, including $m=0$. Such a lifting problem specifies a map to $Q$ on
$$(S\times\Delta^m)\cup(\Delta^n\times\partial\Delta^m).$$
The spine inclusion is inner anodyne by [lem-cbc-spine-inner-anodyne], and the boundary inclusion is degreewise injective. Their pushout product is inner anodyne by [lem-coef-inner-anodyne-pushout-product]. Since $Q$ is a quasicategory, its map to a point is an inner fibration, so the defining lifting property provides an extension to $\Delta^n\times\Delta^m$. Every vertex of $\Delta^n$ belongs to $S$. Therefore every vertical edge at a fixed vertex already belongs to $S\times\Delta^m$ and has its prescribed equivalence image; the extension lies in $Y(\Delta^n)$. This proves the boundary lifting assertion without any extra marking theorem for the spine. By the trivial-fibration characterization of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $r_n$ is a trivial Kan fibration, hence a weak homotopy equivalence.

proof.text: Write $B=Q^\simeq$ and $E=C(Q)_{1,\bullet}$, with source $s$ and target $t$. Let $P_1=E$ and $P_k=P_{k-1}\times_B E$, matching the target of the last edge to $s$. Let $H_1=E$ and $H_k=H_{k-1}\times^h_B E$ with the same endpoint convention and the path model of [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison]. The finite-tower fibrancy lemma applies because both endpoint maps are Kan fibrations by step 2; it gives that all $P_k$ are Kan and retain Kan endpoint maps.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.10, printed p.301; setup of the strict and homotopy Segal pullback towers.

proof.text: The finite-chain comparison lemma gives constant-path maps $c_k:P_k\to H_k$ that are weak homotopy equivalences and commute strictly with the last endpoint. Its induction uses the one-step constant-path comparison for the Kan fibration $s$ and applies homotopy-pullback invariance to $c_{k-1}$, the identity of $E$, and the identity of $B$; the endpoint convention makes both squares commute. Thus $c_n\circ r_n$ is the required consecutive-edge map, and it is a weak homotopy equivalence by composition. The levelwise Kan condition is step 2. Hence these comparisons give exactly the homotopy Segal condition defined in [lem-coef-segal-dk-diagonal-equivalence]. Composition preserves weak homotopy equivalences because it composes the induced component bijections and based homotopy-group isomorphisms.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 4.10, printed p.301, Segal paragraph; finite induction expanded using Kerodon Propositions 3.4.0.7 and 3.4.0.9.

proof.text: For vertices $x,y$ of $Q$, a degree-$m$ simplex in the strict fiber of the endpoint map of step 2 is exactly a map $u:\Delta^1\times\Delta^m\to Q$ whose two endpoint restrictions are the constant simplices at $x,y$. These restrictions have only degenerate edges, hence meet the vertical-equivalence condition automatically. Conversely a simplex of the displayed $U_Q(x,y)$ has precisely these constant endpoint restrictions, and therefore belongs to $C(Q)_{1,m}$. This gives the asserted equality of strict fibers, with simplicial operators inherited from the parameter. Both the endpoint source and its base $B\times B$ are Kan by step 2 (fill product horns coordinatewise). Apply [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] to the endpoint Kan fibration and the point $(x,y)\to B\times B$. The resulting constant-path map identifies this strict fiber up to weak equivalence with the path-space homotopy fiber specified in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. In particular it represents the homotopy fiber, with the actual constant-path comparison and with no change from strict constant endpoints to merely chosen endpoint vertices.

source.place: Section 1, printed p.281 (ordinary morphism space as endpoint fiber), together with Propositions 1.16 and 4.9; the equality with the core endpoint fiber and the path comparison are explicit here.

proof.text: For an $n$-simplex $u$ of the diagonal put $e_Q(u)=u\delta_n$, where $\delta_n:\Delta^n\to\Delta^n\times\Delta^n$ is the diagonal. For every $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ one has $(\Delta(\alpha)\times\Delta(\alpha))\delta_m=\delta_n\Delta(\alpha)$. Hence evaluation commutes with every face and degeneracy, and defines a simplicial map. For $f:Q\to Q'$, $f(u\delta_n)=(fu)\delta_n$ gives its naturality. This clause constructs the specified map only; no weak equivalence assertion for it is used in this proof.
